sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance, forever. Combined with `companion object`, it exists only inside another class, never independently.
sketches.resonance: A companion that can never be duplicated or replaced, bound to exist only within the scope of another — devotion as a language constraint.

sketches.mechanism: Rust's ownership system means passing a value to a function moves it — the caller can no longer use it. The variable is consumed and inaccessible after the call.
sketches.resonance: To give something fully means you no longer have it; the borrow checker enforces the irreversibility of letting go.

sketches.mechanism: A LEFT JOIN preserves every row from the left table even when no matching row exists on the right — the result fills with NULLs where the other side is absent.
sketches.resonance: You remain whole in the result set, but every column where they should have been is NULL — presence shaped entirely by absence.
sketches.draft:
SELECT me.day, them.reply
FROM   every_day  me
LEFT JOIN answers them
ON     me.day = them.day;
